b2-matematikasakk-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Bolyai's Appendix
b2-matematikasakk-01.scenario: At a mathematics evening in Budapest, a student asks what Bolyai Farkas thought of his son's work and what János found.
b2-matematikasakk-01.prompt: Tell her what the father warned his son about and what János discovered anyway.
cues: Say what the father tried to do
Say what János found, however hard it seemed
b2-matematikasakk-01.target: Bármennyire óvta is Bolyai Farkas a fiát, János tovább dolgozott a párhuzamosok problémáján. Az Appendixben egy új, ellentmondásmentes geometriát írt le.
b2-matematikasakk-01.english: However much Farkas Bolyai tried to protect his son, János went on working on the problem of parallels. In the Appendix he described a new, consistent geometry.
b2-matematikasakk-01.canDo: I can explain how János Bolyai worked on Euclid's parallel postulate and what he found.

b2-matematikasakk-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The KöMaL Competition
b2-matematikasakk-02.scenario: At a school evening in Győr about the KöMaL journal, a young visitor asks who could send in solutions and how they were judged.
b2-matematikasakk-02.prompt: Tell him who could send in a solution and what the editors looked at.
cues: Say who could send in a solution
Say what the editors looked at, wherever the letter came from
b2-matematikasakk-02.target: A KöMaL-ba az ország bármelyik középiskolájából bárki beküldhette a megoldását. Bárhonnan érkezett is a levél, a szerkesztők a bizonyítás pontosságát nézték.
b2-matematikasakk-02.english: Anyone from any secondary school in the country could send their solution to KöMaL. Wherever the letter came from, the editors looked at the accuracy of the proof.
b2-matematikasakk-02.canDo: I can explain how the journal KöMaL, founded in 1894, helped to find mathematical talent in Hungary.

b2-matematikasakk-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Erdős Number
b2-matematikasakk-03.scenario: At a talk about Pál Erdős in Budapest, a listener asks how he lived and what the Erdős number means.
b2-matematikasakk-03.prompt: Tell her how Erdős lived and what the Erdős number shows.
cues: Say what the Erdős number shows
b2-matematikasakk-03.target: Akár Párizsban, akár Princetonban járt, Erdős Pál egy kollégájával közösen gondolkodott. Az Erdős-szám azt mutatja meg, hogy valaki hány társszerzői lépésre van tőle.
b2-matematikasakk-03.english: Whether he was in Paris or in Princeton, Pál Erdős thought together with a colleague. The Erdős number shows how many co-author steps someone is from him.
b2-matematikasakk-03.canDo: I can describe Pál Erdős's wandering life, his private vocabulary and the Erdős number.

b2-matematikasakk-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Polgár Experiment
b2-matematikasakk-04.scenario: At the chess club of a Budapest school, a student asks what Polgár László believed and how Judit played.
b2-matematikasakk-04.prompt: Tell him what the father believed about geniuses and how Judit played against strong opponents.
cues: Say how Judit played, whoever sat opposite her
b2-matematikasakk-04.target: Polgár László szerint a zseninek nem születni kell, hanem a zsenit nevelni lehet. Bárki ült is Judittal szemben, ő támadó stílusban játszott.
b2-matematikasakk-04.english: According to László Polgár, a genius does not have to be born but can be raised. Whoever sat opposite Judit, she played in an attacking style.
b2-matematikasakk-04.canDo: I can explain the Polgár family's experiment and Judit Polgár's chess career.

b2-matematikasakk-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Small Nation, Big Ideas
b2-matematikasakk-05.scenario: At a university open day in Budapest, a visitor asks why a small country could do so well in mathematics and chess.
b2-matematikasakk-05.prompt: Tell her what mathematics and chess need and what a talented young person can do.
cues: Say what mathematics and chess do not need
Say what a talented young person can do, however modest the circumstances
b2-matematikasakk-05.target: A matematikához és a sakkhoz nem kell drága berendezés, elég egy ceruza és egy sakktábla. Bármilyen szerény körülmények között él is egy fiatal, a tehetsége utat törhet.
b2-matematikasakk-05.english: Mathematics and chess do not need expensive equipment; a pencil and a chessboard are enough. However modest the circumstances a young person lives in, their talent can make its way.
b2-matematikasakk-05.canDo: I can give reasons why Hungary has done so well in abstract fields such as mathematics and chess.

b2-matematikasakk-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Hungarian Mathematics and Chess
b2-matematikasakk-consolidation.scenario: At a Budapest evening about Hungarian science, a guest asks who Bolyai, Erdős and Polgár Judit were.
b2-matematikasakk-consolidation.prompt: Tell her who they were and what links mathematics and chess in Hungary.
cues: Say who Bolyai and Erdős were
Say what the two fields have in common
b2-matematikasakk-consolidation.target: Bolyai János a nemeuklideszi geometria egyik felfedezője volt, Erdős Pál pedig több mint ötszáz társszerzővel dolgozott. Akár a matematikát, akár a sakkot nézzük, a magyar tehetségek a világ élvonalába kerültek.
b2-matematikasakk-consolidation.english: János Bolyai was one of the discoverers of non-Euclidean geometry, and Pál Erdős worked with more than five hundred co-authors. Whether we look at mathematics or chess, Hungarian talents reached the world's front rank.
b2-matematikasakk-consolidation.canDo: I can discuss the achievements of János Bolyai, the KöMaL tradition, Pál Erdős, and Judit Polgár.
